messages.subject: Error in compareModels?
parts:
Dear all

I wonder whether there is an error in the comparison of models estimated with MLR (i.e. scaled Chi-square difference test). I wrote to the developer of MplusAutomation, but I am not sure he is currently following up on MplusAutomation, since I did not receive an answer.

I compare models with the scaled Chi-square. I developed a formula for that by using the instructions on the Mplus website (you can for instance use Excel). The result I receive is very different from when I use the compareModels function. 
After seeing the discrepancy between my computation and compareModels, I developed the code again (two years after first developing it). The results were the same in my two attempts to develop automatic computation of the scaled Chi-square difference test.

Trouble is, compareModels gives a very different result.

For instance, this is what I get when using code or computing by hand, based on the instruction on the Mplus' site: 
Chi-square diff (21) = 32.5898

This is what compareModels gives as output from comparing the same two models:

MLR Chi-Square Difference Test for Nested Models Based on Loglikelihood
  -----------------------------------------------------------------------

  Difference Test Scaling Correction:  1.1459 
  Chi-square difference:  23.9846 
  Diff degrees of freedom:  21 
  P-value:  0.2938 

  Note: The chi-square difference test assumes that these models are nested.
  It is up to you to verify this assumption.

  MLR Chi-Square Difference test for nested models
  --------------------------------------------

  Difference Test Scaling Correction: 1.1462 
  Chi-square difference: 23.9906 
  Diff degrees of freedom: 21 
  P-value: 0.2935 


I am not sure where the figures for "Difference Test Scaling Correction" are taken from. They appear not to be derived from the H0 Scaling Correction Factors. Anyway, to me the nested Chi-square appears incorrect. 


This is my code for compareModels in MplusAutomation:

parallelModels <- readModels("/...path/ModelCompare")
compareModels(parallelModels[["Model1.out"]],
    parallelModels[["Model2.out"]],
    show=c("diff", "pdiff", "summaries", "unique"), equalityMargin=c(param=.05, pvalue=.02),
    sort="type", diffTest=TRUE, showNS=FALSE)

 
Am I missing something? Or could the code in MplusAutomation be incorrect? If the latter is the case, then it would be important to correct the error to avoid published research using a wrong computation of the scaled Chi-square difference test.  

Kind regards,
Christopher

messages.subject: Re: Error in compareModels?
parts:
Hi Christopher,

Sorry for the delay in getting back to you -- Josh and I do try to keep up on MplusAutomation issues, but it's hard to find time with other competing demands. I reviewed the code for the MLR difference test based on the LL and didn't see anything clearly incorrect. Would you please email me (I don't think Google groups allows attachments) the output files you're using and how you computed the test? I tried to follow the equations here: https://www.statmodel.com/chidiff.shtml. FYI, here's the current R code used for this purpose:

if (m1Summaries$Parameters < m2Summaries$Parameters) {
  H0m <- m1Summaries
  H1m <- m2Summaries
} else {
  H0m <- m2Summaries
  H1m <- m1Summaries
}

if (m1Summaries$Estimator == "MLR") {
  #Chi-square difference test for MLR models based on loglikelihood
  cd <- (H0m$Parameters*H0m$LLCorrectionFactor - H1m$Parameters*H1m$LLCorrectionFactor)/(H0m$Parameters - H1m$Parameters)

  ChiSqDiff <- -2*(H0m$LL - H1m$LL)/cd
  #use difference in the number of parameters for dfDiff since for some models, only LL and Params are available.
  dfDiff <- (H1m$Parameters - H0m$Parameters)

  cat("  MLR Chi-Square Difference Test for Nested Models Based on Loglikelihood  ----------------------------------------------------------------------- ")
  cat("  Difference Test Scaling Correction: ", cd, " ")
  cat("  Chi-square difference: ", round(ChiSqDiff, 4), " ")
  cat("  Diff degrees of freedom: ", dfDiff, " ")
  cat("  P-value: ", round(pchisq(ChiSqDiff, dfDiff, lower.tail=FALSE), 4), " ")
  cat("  Note: The chi-square difference test assumes that these models are nested.  It is up to you to verify this assumption. ")
}

Do you see any problems with the above?

Thanks,
Michael
